candidate_sentences.text: Kvika banki reported a Q2 2026 pre-tax profit of ISK 1,545 million, down ISK 480 million, or 23.7%, from Q2 2025 and 14.6% from Q1 2026.
Net interest income remained resilient, increasing 1.7% to ISK 3,013 million, as higher income from customer lending offset a smaller liquidity portfolio and increased funding costs.
Net fee and commission income fell 26.8% year on year to ISK 1,416 million, reflecting subdued capital-markets activity, lower transaction volumes and weaker client activity.
Administrative expenses declined 1.1% to ISK 2,947 million despite a one-off ISK 112 million restructuring charge.
Efficiency measures reduced employee numbers to 232 and are expected to lower the annual cost base by ISK 300–400 million.

verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Deposits amounted to ISK 201.2 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by 16.5% from year-end 2025. Loans to customers amounted to ISK 223.3 bn. at the end of Q2 2026, increasing by ISK 15.8 bn., or 7.6%, from year-end 2025.

candidate_sentences.text: Balance-sheet growth continued, with loans to customers up 7.6% from year-end 2025 to ISK 223.3 billion and deposits up 16.5% to ISK 201.2 billion.

verified_key_information_units.information: Capital adequacy ratio (CAR) stood at 23.0% at 30 June 2026, down from 26.8% at year-end 2025 primarily due to the ISK 10.2 billion special dividend payment in June, while maintaining a strong management buffer above regulatory requirements.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: CAR of 23.0% at 30 June 2026, decreasing as special dividend was distributed in June. The bank continues to target a management buffer of 2% to 4% over current and anticipated CAR requirements.
